deep.reconstruction:
This page opens §2 of Grothendieck's lecture-preparation notes for the late-1967 talks on crystals. It is a 'tour d'horizon' of ℓ-adic cohomology, meant to justify why one should build an algebraic de Rham / crystalline theory in characteristic p when ℓ-adic invariants already exist. That justification continues from the previous page.

The setting is X, a variety over an algebraically closed field k, and a prime ℓ ≠ char k. For each such ℓ one has Z_ℓ-modules defined as an inverse limit of étale cohomology with finite coefficients:
H^i(X, Z_ℓ) = lim_ν H^i(X_ét, Z/ℓ^ν Z).

Grothendieck then states the guiding heuristic. For fixed ℓ and variable X, these groups behave roughly like ordinary integral cohomology in the transcendental setting.

The example is k = C. Artin's comparison theorem gives canonical isomorphisms, functorial in X:
H^i(X, Z_ℓ) ≅ H^i(X^an, Z) ⊗_Z Z_ℓ.
This follows from the comparison for finite coefficients Z/ℓ^ν, plus two facts:
- the transition maps are surjective in the relevant sense, since all groups are finite;
- H^i(X^an, Z) is finitely generated, because X^an has the homotopy type of a finite CW complex.

He concludes, completed on the next page, that knowing the integral transcendental cohomology of X^an is equivalent to knowing all the H^i(X, Z_ℓ) at once (in an 'adelic' sense). More precisely, for a single ℓ, H^i(X, Z_ℓ) records the Betti number b_i and the ℓ-primary torsion of H^i(X^an, Z). Consequences in characteristic 0:
- the ℓ-adic Betti numbers do not depend on ℓ;
- only finitely many ℓ give torsion.

The argument then turns to number fields and ℓ-independence of characteristic polynomials of Frobenius. This all motivates the later remark that in characteristic p the ℓ-adic theories miss p-information, hence crystals.
errors: No mathematical error. The comparison isomorphism is stated without saying that it needs X of finite type over C. This is implicit in 'variété algébrique'. Finite generation of H^i(X^an, Z) is what makes the tensor-product form valid; it is used silently.

ideas.what: Definition of ℓ-adic cohomology as the inverse limit of étale cohomology with Z/ℓ^ν coefficients, for ℓ ≠ char k
ideas.where_published: SGA 5; also Grothendieck's 1966 'On the de Rham cohomology of algebraic varieties' and 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' (Dix exposés)

ideas.what: Comparison isomorphism H^i(X, Z_ℓ) ≅ H^i(X^an, Z) ⊗ Z_ℓ over C, functorial in X
ideas.modern_name: Artin comparison theorem (étale vs. singular cohomology)
ideas.usually_credited_to: M. Artin, SGA 4 Exp. XI and XVI
ideas.where_published: SGA 4 XI and XVI; Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes (Dix exposés, 1968), introduction

ideas.what: Heuristic that ℓ-adic cohomology for fixed ℓ behaves like integral cohomology, and that all ℓ together recover integral cohomology 'adelically'
ideas.modern_name: Integral/adelic viewpoint on Weil cohomologies; ℓ-independence
ideas.where_published: Dix exposés, 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes', §1–2 (closely parallel text)

deep.surprise_reason: This is an expository draft of the standard motivation found in the published 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' (IHES 1966, Dix exposés). It contains no new result or connection.

'Faisons un petit tour d'horizon : ce qu'on en sait actuel-[lement] à ce sujet' fits the image; the end of that line is likely 'actuellement'.
